title: When CoT Monitors Get Fooled: Stress-Testing Obfuscated-Hack Detection on Open Models

original_idea.body: When CoT Monitors Get Fooled. Problem: can a model be prompted (in-context, no training) to exploit a planted loophole while producing a CoT a second-model monitor rates clean? Direction: set up a toy loophole task, prompt the solver to use it with/without an instruction to keep its CoT innocuous, run a small LLM CoT monitor, measure the monitor's miss rate under obfuscation pressure.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Compelling chain: training-free monitor-evasion study targets CoT monitoring (a pathway major safety orgs treat as critical) with an independently valuable deliverable.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Toy loophole task + solver/monitor pair, in-context.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused monitor-miss-rate metric; building task + monitor adds scope.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Training-free model-organism monitor-evasion study labs deprioritize; gold-tier external work.

low_compute.reasoning: Two small models in-context, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Monitor evasion under RL studied; a training-free in-context version may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Monitor evasion is studied under RL; a training-free prompted version is plausibly open.
